subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Nanostructures in Vaccines
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on DNA Nanostructures in Vaccines.

hook.text: Arrange antigens on a DNA scaffold at precise distances and the immune response jumps — geometry shapes immunity.

buildup.text: B cells recognize multivalent displays — clustering antigens at optimal spacing crosslinks B cell receptors efficiently.

discovery.text: DNA origami places antigens at exact 5 to 30 nm spacing — revealing the optimal distance for maximum immune activation.

twist.text: DNA itself is an immune stimulant — CpG motifs on the origami act as built-in adjuvants, boosting the response further.

climax.text: Preclinical studies show DNA origami vaccines producing stronger antibody responses than soluble antigen alone.

punchline.text: Spacing antigens precisely on DNA scaffolds — geometry makes better vaccines.

quiz.question: Why does antigen spacing on DNA origami improve immune responses?
options: Antigens dissolve faster when attached to DNA
Precise spacing crosslinks B cell receptors optimally, and CpG motifs on DNA act as built-in adjuvants
DNA origami prevents antigens from reaching immune cells
